title: A reducing move lowers the height by exactly one
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If a diagram $D'$ is obtained from an oriented diagram $D$ by a Yamada-Vogel reducing move, then $h(D')=h(D)-1$. Consequently every sequence of reducing moves starting at $D$ has length at most $h(D)$.
strategy: Write $A$ for the annulus cobounded by the incoherent pair $C_i,C_j$, and let $D_i,D_j$ be the two complementary disks; after the move the pair is replaced by a coherent pair $C_a,C_z$ joined by two opposite signed arcs, where $C_a$ bounds a disk in the new picture and $C_z$ bounds the disk containing all circles of the original annulus. For every third circle $C_p$ compare its coherence with the new circles using the region that contains it: the substitutions produce exactly one fewer incoherent pair, and the moved pair itself becomes coherent. This is the complete bookkeeping argument of the survey's Lemma 2.1 (and of Traczyk's paragraph after Figure 2). The bookkeeping argument consumes the annulus lemma through the coherence of the two replaced circles and of every third circle, so the AC hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the two-circle separation lemma.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
